corrections.source_problem: The explanatory sentence lists values for object and function variables, omitting the relation-variable assignments defined immediately above.
corrections.target_action: The Gujarati explanation names all three assigned kinds, with an adjacent sourcecorrection note.

corrections.source_problem: The prose's reciprocal nonmembership wording states only disjointness, while the displayed biconditional requires the two relations to be complements over the whole domain.
corrections.target_action: The Gujarati explanation states the all-domain biconditional and complement relation, with an adjacent sourcecorrection note.

corrections.source_problem: The prose initially defines enumerable for an arbitrary set but its m0 and z∈M characterization requires a nonempty set; standard structures here have nonempty domains.
corrections.target_action: The Gujarati local definition explicitly scopes the argument to a nonempty set with an adjacent note.

corrections.source_problem: A finite orbit under f repeats its last fixed member although the listed enumeration is stated without repetitions; the forward proof also omits f's value on the last finite member.
corrections.target_action: The Gujarati text takes distinct orbit members and explicitly fixes the final finite member in the forward proof, with an adjacent note.

corrections.source_problem: The final formula writes its bound object variable once as \Obj v_0 and once as unadorned v_0.
corrections.target_action: Both occurrences visibly use the established bound-variable notation \Obj{v_0}; the adjacent Gujarati sourcecorrection explains the departure.

corrections.source_problem: The first two successor axioms plus full induction characterize the zero-successor reduct but do not constrain arbitrary preinterpreted +, ×, or ≤ symbols.
corrections.target_action: The Gujarati proposition explicitly speaks of formulas defining the standard operations in the successor-only basis, with a visible adjacent note.

corrections.source_problem: The displayed addition formula binds w but writes u(x′)=u(x)′ in the recursion clause, leaving w unused and failing to express the required all-input recursion.
corrections.target_action: The Gujarati displayed formula writes u(w′)=u(w)′, and the adjacent note identifies the frozen-source defect.

corrections.source_problem: Without an effectivity condition, the set of all valid SOL sentences itself supplies a trivially sound and complete but noncomputable axiom set.
corrections.target_action: The theorem says no effectively specified sound complete derivation system exists, with a visible adjacent note.

corrections.source_problem: In the displayed satisfaction expression the closing brace for Sat's second argument falls outside math mode, and the intended all-structures scope is implicit.
corrections.target_action: The Gujarati formula places the brace inside math mode and explicitly says every structure, with an adjacent note.

corrections.source_problem: The step from an enumeration of sentences to a first-order definable truth set leaves the Gödel coding of sentence outputs implicit.
corrections.target_action: The Gujarati explanation identifies y as a sentence Gödel number and records that coding in an adjacent note.

corrections.source_problem: The compactness theorem reuses thm:sol-undecidable, already assigned to the preceding undecidability theorem.
corrections.target_action: The Gujarati theorem has the distinct label thm:sol-not-compact, with an adjacent note.

corrections.source_problem: In the finite-subset proof, the claim that no A^{≥n} with n>k occurs in the full Γ is false: Γ contains every such sentence.
corrections.target_action: The Gujarati argument bounds only the chosen finite Γ0 and handles a subset without size demands by taking k≥1, with an adjacent note.

corrections.source_problem: The no-larger-than formula requires u to be injective on the full domain, although only u restricted to X is needed to witness an injection X→Y.
corrections.target_action: The Gujarati formula restricts the injectivity antecedent to x,y∈X, with an adjacent note.

corrections.source_problem: The equinumerosity formula requires u to be globally injective. If X is a proper subset of an infinite domain M and Y=M while X≈Y, a bijection X→Y cannot extend to a globally injective u:M→M.
corrections.target_action: The Gujarati formula requires injectivity only for arguments in X, with an adjacent note.

corrections.source_problem: Inf(X) omits closure u[X]⊆X and a final closing parenthesis. A two-element domain with singleton X and a swap permutation satisfies the source formula although X is finite.
corrections.target_action: The Gujarati formula adds closure on X, the closing parenthesis and an adjacent counterexample note.

corrections.source_problem: Count(X) concludes X=Y for every u-closed Y containing z; choosing Y as the whole domain forces X to be the whole domain, contrary to the stated subset characterization. The original also excludes the empty subset.
corrections.target_action: The Gujarati formula concludes X⊆Y and adds an empty-set disjunct, with an adjacent note.

corrections.source_problem: The proposed Aleph_1 criterion says every subset Y⊆X is finite or Aleph_0, yet Y=X and X is claimed uncountable; it is contradictory. The macro subscript is also inconsistent with Aleph_0.
corrections.target_action: The Gujarati text characterizes minimal uncountable size by requiring every uncountable subset of X to be equinumerous with X, and normalizes the macro subscript, with an adjacent note.

corrections.source_problem: The second conjunct of Pow(Y,R,X) lacks a closing parenthesis for the implication beginning Y(x), leaving the displayed formula's round delimiters unbalanced.
corrections.target_action: The Gujarati display adds the missing closing parenthesis and an adjacent note.

corrections.source_problem: The proof's final line mentions subsets of s(Z), although Z is not the fixed countably infinite set; the intended set is s(X). It also contains an English typo.
corrections.target_action: The Gujarati proof uses s(X), with an adjacent note.

corrections.source_problem: The claimed domain-continuum formula only requires a power-set code set Y to lie in the range of an injective domain self-map. The identity map makes the range condition trivial; duplicate codes also remain possible, so domains larger than the continuum can satisfy it.
corrections.target_action: The Gujarati formula requires Cont(Y) and requires Y to equal the range of an injective total u:Domain(M)→Domain(M), with an adjacent note.
